_comment: T3-CREATURES. The four NEW SPECIES from docs/owner-direction/TETHERBOUND_MEADOWS_CREATURE_EXPANSION.md whose build path is a new Meshy mesh, authored in full except for that mesh. NOTHING LOADS THIS FILE. It is not a parallel species system and must never become one: scripts/creatures/creature_species.gd reads data/creatures/species.json and only that. This exists because two rules meet head-on. (1) tests/smoke_art.gd asserts that EVERY entry in species.json names a `placeholder.model` that exists on disk, and species.json's own _comment_wild_roster already states the resulting rule -- 'Species appear in this file as each is produced'. (2) tools/art_pipeline/meshy.py reads MESHY_API_KEY from the environment and nowhere else, and no key is set in this session, so these four meshes cannot be generated here. Putting them in species.json with an empty or invented model path would break a real test, and weakening that test to accept a missing mesh would destroy the only thing standing between this project and a creature that renders as a fallback capsule in front of the owner. So the design work landed here instead, complete, and the MESH IS THE ONE OPEN FIELD.
_comment_how_to_land_one: When a MESHY_API_KEY exists: generate the mesh from that creature's sheet in docs/art/reference/creature-expansion-2026-08-30/, install it under assets/creatures/tetherbound/<id>/models/, set `placeholder.model` below to that path, MOVE the whole entry into data/creatures/species.json's `species` object, and add its spawn clusters using the `pending_spawn_plan` block each entry carries. Nothing else about the entry should need to change -- typing, stats, moves, catch rate, behaviour, scale and the spawn plan are all decided here. Delete the entry from this file in the same commit so the two can never disagree.
_comment_scale: Heights are the owner's master-sheet SIZE GUIDE ('Relative to Player ~1.8m'), which the lane brief names authoritative for scale. That guide can be checked against the game because it also lists three creatures that already exist: Bramblebun 1.0m (game 0.96m), Paddlenewt 1.1m (game 1.15m) and Trailpup 1.2m (game 1.28m) -- all three within 6%, so the guide's numbers ARE game scale for this biome and are used directly. Sparkit is the one adjustment: the guide says 0.8m, which would put it below Pipwing's 0.76m and collide with its own sheet's insistence that it is 'NOT tiny or difficult to see... roughly large fox / small coyote scale', so it is authored at 0.85m -- still the second-smallest creature in the game. Radius scales with height at the band's usual ratio, per D12, so nothing is easier to hit relative to its own size. The guide ALSO disagrees with the game on two creatures this lane did not change: it puts Burrowback at 2.6m against a shipped 1.70m, and Tuskroot at 2.6m against 2.15m. See ralph/reports/handover-T3-CREATURES-2026-08-30.md -- that is an owner question, not something to fix silently here.

sparkit._why: Sheet 3, brief section 3. Pure Electric, 'fast striker' -- the highest attack-to-defence ratio in the game (2.0) and the second-lowest defence, which is the brief's 'noticeably quicker and more aggressive than most early Ground creatures' expressed as a statline rather than as a speed stat this build does not have. `aggressive` is FALSE: the brief gives it no hostile behaviour, and in this build that flag means specifically 'will start a fight on its own' (GAME_DESIGN.md 14).

pending_spawn_plan.geography: open Meadows and disturbed technological areas; NOT deep forest
pending_spawn_plan._note: The brief's '~2% ordinary, 5-8% during storms' is a per-encounter-roll number and this build has no encounter roll -- see the handover. Expressed instead as SIX individuals across three bands, of which four sit behind a rain weather gate and two are ungated. That reproduces the intended experience directly: in clear weather Sparkit is a 2-in-881 creature, and rain roughly triples what is out there. The lesson the brief wants -- 'storms are worth exploring' -- is a property of the gate, not of a percentage. THE BRIEF'S 'STORM' DOES NOT EXIST IN THIS BUILD: data/config/weather.json declares exactly four presets -- clear, cloudy, fog, rain -- and scripts/world/world_weather.gd's header states 'thunderstorms are explicitly out of scope here'. `rain` is used as the nearest existing weather; when a storm preset exists, name it here instead and nothing else needs to change.

cindercub._why: Sheet 4, brief section 4. Fire/Ground, 'balanced' role and the most even statline of the new creatures on purpose -- the brief asks for 'personality rather than simply functioning as an enemy'. `aggressive` FALSE: 'curious; moderately territorial; not automatically hyper-aggressive... sometimes resting/sleeping near warm objects'. Its charged is Ground (`rootquake`) against a Fire quick so both halves of its typing are visible in play.

pending_spawn_plan.geography: ONLY near sources of warmth. Explicitly never wetland or pond.
pending_spawn_plan._note: Brief says '1-2% of qualifying warm-area wildlife spawns'. The qualifying habitat barely exists yet: the Meadows has no authored geothermal or scorched terrain outside Team Tether's industrial sites in bands 4-5. Three individuals, all at Tether industrial ground, is the honest read of '1-2% of a very small eligible set' -- and it makes the creature's presence mean something (Team Tether's works are warm) instead of scattering Fire through a Ground biome.

shadelet._why: Sheet 5, brief section 5. Pure Dark, 'stealth/balanced'. The sheet is emphatic that it must NOT be tiny -- 'roughly monitor-lizard / medium dog length... must read clearly from normal gameplay camera distance' -- so 1.60m, larger than Trailpup and Mosshell and just under Burrowback. `footprint_allowance` is 4.0, the highest in the game: this is a long-bodied lizard with a 'long tail for balance' per the sheet, and creature_body._fit() would otherwise scale the whole model DOWN to fit a quadruped-shaped allowance. `aggressive` FALSE -- 'cautious; stalks around cover; may freeze and watch player; moderate aggression rather than charging immediately'.

pending_spawn_plan.geography: dark sheltered ground; Burrow Warrens perimeter and forest edge
pending_spawn_plan._note: Brief: '3-5% of qualifying dark-habitat spawns at night; close to zero in daylight except inside caves'. This is the ONE creature in the expansion whose numbers survive translation unchanged, because the existing `time: night` gate does exactly what the brief describes -- eight individuals present at night and gone by day. Band 2's warrens and band 3's gorge shade are the qualifying ground. It is the most common of the five new species by design; 'uncommon' in the brief's own ladder is 5-10%, not 1-3%.

frostclaw._why: Sheet 9, brief section 9. Pure Ice, 'agile striker' and the only new species with `aggressive` TRUE: 'Predator. Solitary; stalks prey; observes player from distance; territorial if approached; fast burst movement.' Second-highest attack in the wild roster after Stormtrail, and 2.00m makes it the third-largest wild creature -- 'larger than Bramblebun and Sparkit, smaller than the largest Alpha predators', which is exactly where the size guide puts it.

pending_spawn_plan.geography: GEOGRAPHICALLY CONSTRAINED, and this is the load-bearing part of its design. The brief: 'Frostclaw is NOT native to the central Meadows. It enters from the direction of the future Frozen Mountains / severed cold-region road... its presence should make ecological/story sense.' Confine to the highest, coldest band-4/5 edge nearest the severed northern road. Never the starting fields, never the pond valley.
pending_spawn_plan._note: Brief: '1-2% of eligible cold-edge spawns. Potentially one active Frostclaw in the broader Meadows region at a time.' Those two sentences disagree slightly and the second is the stronger intent, so: TWO individuals, both weather-gated, at opposite ends of the cold edge, so at most one is present in any weather the player is standing in. That satisfies 'one active at a time' without needing a runtime singleton the architecture does not have. Weather gate is ['rain','fog'] -- the brief asks for 'rain, cold-looking weather, fog, unusual Rift/weather events if supported', and fog is the closest thing this build has to cold-looking weather. There is no storm preset; see the sparkit note.

_comment_bramblebun_redesign: Brief section 6 is the FIFTH mesh-blocked item and it is NOT in the table above, because Bramblebun already exists as a species: it needs a replacement MESH for the same canonical id, not a new entry. 'Do not simply recolor or resize the existing Bramblebun. The existing implementation is visually too small and too generic. This is a replacement asset for the same canonical species.' When a key exists, generate from sheet 06 and repoint species.json:bramblebun.placeholder.model at the new .glb; no other field needs to move. One measurement worth having before someone does: the brief says 'increase its size substantially', but the owner's OWN size guide on the master sheet puts Bramblebun at 1.0m against a shipped 0.96m -- a 4% difference, not a substantial one. Those two statements are only compatible if 'size' there means visual MASS rather than height, which is also what the sheet's own note says ('Larger and more substantial') and what the artwork shows: a heavy, bramble-covered hare with oversized ears at the same standing height. So the bulk must come from the MESH, and whoever lands it should not also inflate `height` to chase the word 'substantially' -- that would take the creature off the owner's own size guide. This lane moved `height` 0.96 -> 1.00 to sit exactly on the guide and did nothing else, because the rest is genuinely mesh work.
